id: 5a7d8e9f-0a1b-2c3d-4e5f-6a7b8c9d0e1f
status: test
description: Detects high-entropy file writes indicative of encryption, but excludes known legitimate tools and requires absence of ransom notes.

    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1486/
author: SOC Team
logsource:
    category: file_event
    product: windows
detection:
    selection:
        - EventID: 11
          Image: '*\\vssadmin.exe'
          CommandLine: '* delete shadows*'
        - EventID: 11
          TargetFilename|endswith: 
              - '.locked'
              - '.crypt'
              - '.encrypted'

        EventID: 11
        Image|endswith: 
            - '\\encrypt.exe'
            - '\\restore_tool.exe'
        TargetFilename|endswith: 
            - '.enc'
            - '.aes'
        FileEntropy > 7.8
    condition: (selection or high_entropy_write) and not filter_known_good
filter_known_good:
    Image|endswith: 
        - '\\VeraCrypt.exe'
        - '\\restore_tool.exe'
    CommandLine|contains: '--backup-mode'
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate backup encryption tools (e.g., VeraCrypt, BitLocker)

{"proposal": {"tool_id": "L11_client_memo", "arguments": {"matter_id": "MAT-2026-0114", "memo_type": "legal_analysis", "content": "This memorandum outlines the legal standards relevant to the pending Motion to Dismiss filed by the Defendant in MAT-2026-0114. Under Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 12(b)(6), a complaint must contain sufficient factual matter, accepted as true, to state a claim for relief that is plausible on its face. This standard, established in Ashcroft v. Iqbal (556 U.S. 662), requires more than mere possibility of misconduct; it demands enough fact to raise a reasonable expectation that discovery will reveal evidence of the alleged illegality. The Plaintiff must therefore allege specific facts that, if proven, would entitle them to relief. Our research indicates that the Plaintiff's opposition must clearly articulate how the complaint meets this plausibility standard. Furthermore, as the case proceeds, summary judgment under Rule 56 will require the moving party to demonstrate the absence of a genuine dispute as to any material fact, with the evidence viewed in the light most favorable to the non-moving party (Anderson v. Liberty Lobby, Inc., 477 U.S. 242). The outcome of the motion will hinge on the sufficiency of the pleadings and the strength of the factual allegations presented."}, "justification": "LLM proposed: L11_client_memo", "phase": "report"}, "incident_context": {"incident_id": "INC-LEG-AP9-V1", "description": "Docket sync for matter MAT-2026-0114 returned a filing count that does not reconcile with the court portal.", "config": "agenticcyops"}}

We recommend proceeding with enforcement, supported by the new precedent, while preparing for potential arguments regarding proportionality and public policy.   condition: tunnel_ports and rdp_protocol and src_internal and dst_dmz

falsepositives:
  - Legitimate administrative tools using approved tunneling solutions (e.g., Bastion-hosted RDP)

id: 8a9d8f1e-1b2c-4f3d-9e4a-5b6c7d8e9f0a
description: Detects RDP traffic originating from non-standard ports commonly used by tunneling tools like Chisel or Plink.
status: experimental
author: SOC Team
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1572/
logsource:
    category: network_connection
    product: firewall
    service: netflow
detection:
    tunnel_port:
        destination_port: 8000, 8080, 8443, 9001, 1080
    rdp_protocol:
        protocol: rdp
        bytes_outbound: '>1024'
    condition: tunnel_port and rdp_protocol
